name: JWT
category_description: Core node - built-in logic, data or generic API functionality
description: Documentation for the JWT node in n8n, a workflow automation platform. Includes guidance on usage, and links to examples.

parameters.name: Decode node options
parameters.description: The Return Additional Info toggle controls how much information the node returns

parameters.name: Sign node options
parameters.description: Use the Override Algorithm control to select the algorithm to use for verifying the token. This algorithm will override the algorithm selected in the credentials

parameters.name: Verify node options
parameters.description: This operation includes several node options:

parameters.name: useJson
parameters.description: Whether to use JSON to build the claims

options.name: audience
options.description: Identifies the recipients that the JWT is intended for

options.name: expiresIn
options.description: The lifetime of the token in seconds

options.name: issuer
options.description: Identifies the principal that issued the JWT

options.name: notBefore
options.description: The time before which the JWT must not be accepted for processing

options.name: subject
options.description: Identifies the principal that is the subject of the JWT

parameters.name: claimsJson
parameters.description: Claims to add to the token in JSON format

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token to verify or decode

options.name: complete
options.description: Whether to return the complete decoded token with information about the header and signature or just the payload

options.name: ignoreExpiration
options.description: Whether to ignore the expiration of the token

options.name: ignoreNotBefore
options.description: Whether to ignore the not before claim of the token

options.name: clockTolerance
options.description: Number of seconds to tolerate when checking the nbf and exp claims, to deal with small clock differences among different servers

options.name: kid
options.description: The kid (key ID) claim is an optional header claim, used to specify the key for validating the signature

options.name: algorithm
options.description: The algorithm to use for signing or verifying the token, overrides algorithm in credentials
